name: Corteva, Inc.
domainRelevance: Corteva is the world's largest pure-play seed company and a top-three global crop-protection manufacturer, with integrated platforms in corn, soybean, and specialty crops. The company's seed genetics and chemical herbicide/insecticide portfolios directly set input costs for 300+ million acres of North American row-crop production, making it a primary price-setter in the agricultural value chain. Corteva's margin cycles and inventory turns are leading indicators of farmer profitability and acreage decisions.
portalRelevance: Corteva's quarterly seed sales, crop-protection volumes, and pricing power are critical forward signals for agricultural commodity prices, farm equipment demand (Deere, AGCO), and downstream food-system inflation. The company's debt trajectory and free-cash-flow generation under commodity-price stress are material to agricultural-credit risk and rural-economy health. Corteva's R&D spending and M&A activity (e.g., Brevant acquisition) signal sector consolidation and trait-adoption velocity.

notes.cohortStatus: Anchor agriscience company; peer group includes Bayer CropScience, BASF, Syngenta (ChemChina subsidiary)

intelligenceCycle.name: Signal Capture
items: Quarterly seed sales volume and pricing by crop (corn, soybean, specialty) disclosed in 10-Q segment revenue
Crop-protection herbicide/insecticide shipment trends and price realization vs. commodity input costs (crude oil, phosphate)
8-K announcements of supply-chain disruptions, tariff impacts, or customer concentration changes (e.g., major retailer contract renewals)
USDA acreage reports and farmer-sentiment indices (USDA Ag Prices, NASS) as demand leading indicators

intelligenceCycle.name: State Estimation
items: Rolling 4-quarter free-cash-flow trajectory and working-capital swings tied to seed-season timing (Q1–Q2 peak)
Debt-to-EBITDA ratio and interest-coverage stress under commodity-price downturns (corn/soybean prices <$4/$10)
Gross-margin compression from input-cost inflation (phosphate, potash, crude oil) vs. pricing-power lag to farmers
R&D pipeline maturity (trait-stack adoption rates, regulatory approvals for new herbicide modes) as competitive-position signal

intelligenceCycle.name: Diagnosis
items: Pattern match: seed-margin compression + inventory buildup + farmer-credit stress = demand cliff risk (historical: 2015–2016 farm crisis)
Competitive delta: Corteva's corn-seed market share vs. Bayer/Monsanto legacy position; herbicide-resistance trait adoption velocity vs. Syngenta
Regulatory risk: EPA herbicide-use restrictions (dicamba, glyphosate litigation) as revenue-headwind trigger; trait-approval delays from USDA-APHIS
Sector contagion: Corteva distress → Deere demand cliff → CNH Industrial / AGCO margin compression → rural-bank credit losses

intelligenceCycle.name: Regulation
items: Investment thesis: long Corteva on trait-adoption tailwinds + farmer-profitability recovery; short on commodity-price downside + debt refinancing risk
Risk hedge: short corn/soybean futures to hedge seed-volume exposure; long phosphate/potash to offset input-cost inflation pass-through lag
Engagement: monitor board-level ESG commitments (carbon-neutral seed production, pollinator-safety programs) as regulatory-risk proxy for EPA/state actions
Dividend sustainability: track free-cash-flow coverage of 3–4% dividend yield under stress scenarios (commodity prices -20%)

intelligenceCycle.name: Action
items: Trade execution: establish position size based on Q1 seed-sales guidance vs. farmer-acreage expectations; rebalance on 10-Q earnings surprise
Portfolio rebalancing: reduce Corteva weight if debt-to-EBITDA exceeds 3.5x; increase on trait-approval catalyst (USDA deregulation of new stack)
Engagement strategy: quarterly earnings-call monitoring for management commentary on farmer-credit stress, retailer contract terms, and input-cost pass-through
Operational response: track supply-chain announcements (manufacturing capacity, logistics partnerships) for margin-expansion or disruption signals

intelligenceCycle.name: Feedback
items: Earnings validation: compare Q+1 seed-sales volume vs. USDA acreage forecast; gross margin vs. commodity-input-cost index (WPU012)
Price action: monitor CTVA stock reaction to USDA crop-progress reports, farmer-sentiment surveys, and competitor earnings (Bayer, BASF)
Filing delta: track 10-Q changes in allowance-for-doubtful-accounts (farmer-credit risk), inventory reserves (demand weakness), and debt covenant disclosures
Thesis validation: compare realized free-cash-flow vs. model prediction; assess dividend-cut risk if FCF turns negative for 2+ quarters

intelligenceCycle.name: Adaptation
items: Model update: recalibrate seed-volume elasticity to commodity prices based on realized Q-over-Q acreage changes and farmer-profitability data
Signal reweight: increase weight on USDA acreage reports and farmer-credit indices if they outpredict earnings surprises vs. analyst consensus
Sector prior update: adjust agricultural-input-cost inflation priors based on Corteva's realized input-cost pass-through rates and customer-mix shifts
Competitive calibration: update market-share assumptions for corn seed and herbicides based on trait-adoption data and regulatory approval timelines

functionalNetwork.model: Corteva operates as a distributed decision-making system across seed genetics, crop-protection chemistry, and commercial operations. The company's seed R&D and trait-stack pipeline function as a long-cycle strategic cortex, while crop-protection manufacturing and logistics operate as a high-velocity operational motor. Farmer demand signals (acreage, commodity prices, credit availability) feed through retailer and distributor networks into inventory and pricing decisions. Regulatory approval cycles (EPA, USDA-APHIS) act as external constraint-setters on product launches. Debt and capital-allocation decisions reflect commodity-price volatility and competitive positioning, creating feedback loops between financial health and market share.

suppliers.name: Mosaic Company
suppliers.relationshipNote: Mosaic supplies phosphate and potash fertilizer inputs to Corteva's crop-protection formulations and seed-treatment products. Phosphate and potash represent 8–12% of Corteva's COGS in crop-protection segment. Mosaic's pricing power and supply disruptions (mine shutdowns, export restrictions) directly compress Corteva's gross margins; Corteva typically lags 1–2 quarters in passing through price increases to farmers. Disclosed in 10-K Item 1A supply-chain risk factors.

suppliers.name: Huntsman Corporation
suppliers.relationshipNote: Huntsman supplies titanium dioxide and specialty chemical intermediates used in Corteva's herbicide and insecticide manufacturing. Huntsman's production capacity constraints and pricing (tied to crude oil and sulfuric acid costs) create margin volatility for Corteva's crop-protection segment. Corteva's 10-K discloses reliance on limited suppliers for key chemical feedstocks; Huntsman is a primary source for dicamba and glyphosate precursors.

suppliers.name: Nufarm Americas
suppliers.relationshipNote: Nufarm supplies generic herbicide active pharmaceutical ingredients (glyphosate, atrazine) to Corteva's formulation operations, particularly for lower-margin commodity products. Nufarm's capacity and pricing are sensitive to Chinese and Indian API export restrictions and tariffs. Corteva uses Nufarm as a secondary source to manage supply risk and cost, but. Relationship disclosed in supply-chain risk sections of 10-K.

suppliers.name: Valent U.S.A. Corporation
suppliers.relationshipNote: Valent (Sumitomo subsidiary) supplies specialty insecticide and fungicide formulations for Corteva's specialty-crop portfolio (vegetables, fruits, ornamentals). Valent's product pipeline and regulatory approvals (EPA Section 3 registrations) influence Corteva's ability to expand specialty-crop margins. Relationship is primarily distribution and co-development; disclosed in 10-K segment disclosures.

suppliers.name: Clariant AG
suppliers.relationshipNote: Clariant supplies seed-treatment fungicides and insecticides (nematicides, biologics) used in Corteva's seed-coating operations. Clariant's innovation in biological seed treatments (Bacillus, Trichoderma strains) is a competitive differentiator for Corteva's premium seed offerings. Corteva's 10-K discloses reliance on specialty chemical suppliers for trait-enabling seed treatments; Clariant is a key innovation partner.

suppliers.name: Lyondell Basell Industries
suppliers.relationshipNote: Lyondell Basell supplies polyethylene and polypropylene resins for Corteva's seed-bag, chemical-container, and agricultural-film packaging. Crude-oil price volatility directly impacts Lyondell's resin pricing, which flows through to Corteva's packaging COGS (estimated 3–5% of total COGS). Corteva's 10-K discloses exposure to petroleum-based input costs; Lyondell is a primary source. Supply-chain risk disclosed in Item 1A.

suppliers.name: Tronox Holdings plc
suppliers.relationshipNote: Tronox supplies titanium dioxide pigments used in Corteva's herbicide and insecticide formulations for color stability and UV protection. Tronox's production (chloride and sulfate processes) is energy-intensive and sensitive to natural-gas prices. Corteva's 10-K discloses reliance on limited suppliers for specialty pigments; Tronox is a primary source. Pricing is negotiated annually; recent contracts reflect 15–20% price increases (2021–2023).

suppliers.name: Univar Solutions Inc.
suppliers.relationshipNote: Univar Solutions is a major distributor of Corteva's crop-protection chemicals to regional agricultural retailers and cooperatives in North America. Univar manages inventory, order fulfillment, and logistics for ~15–20% of Corteva's crop-protection volume. Univar's warehouse capacity and transportation costs (fuel, labor) directly impact Corteva's supply-chain efficiency and customer-service levels. Relationship disclosed in 10-K customer-concentration and distribution-channel sections.

suppliers.name: Soy Energy LLC
suppliers.relationshipNote: Soy Energy (joint venture between Cargill and Western Iowa Energy) supplies soybean oil and meal co-products used in Corteva's seed-coating and adjuvant formulations. Soybean oil prices are volatile and tied to commodity soybean prices; Corteva uses soy-based adjuvants as a sustainable alternative to petroleum-based surfactants. Relationship reflects Corteva's sustainability commitments disclosed in ESG reports.

suppliers.name: J.B. Hunt Transport Services, Inc.
suppliers.relationshipNote: J.B. Hunt operates Corteva's primary long-haul trucking network for seed and crop-protection distribution from manufacturing plants to regional distribution centers and customer warehouses. J.B. Hunt handles ~25–30% of Corteva's domestic logistics volume. Fuel surcharges and driver-wage inflation directly impact Corteva's distribution costs (estimated 8–10% of COGS). Corteva's 10-K discloses reliance on third-party logistics; J.B. Hunt is a named strategic partner in supply-chain disclosures.

suppliers.name: Maersk Line Limited
suppliers.relationshipNote: Maersk operates Corteva's international ocean-freight network for seed and crop-protection exports to Latin America, Europe, and Asia-Pacific regions. Maersk handles ~40–50% of Corteva's international logistics volume. Container-rate volatility and port congestion directly impact Corteva's export margins and customer-delivery timelines. Corteva's 10-K discloses international revenue (~30% of total) and reliance on ocean freight; Maersk is a primary carrier.

logisticsPartners.name: XPO Logistics, Inc.
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: XPO Logistics operates Corteva's regional distribution and last-mile delivery network, particularly for specialty-crop and high-value seed products requiring temperature control and expedited handling. XPO manages ~15–20% of Corteva's domestic distribution volume. XPO's labor costs and fleet utilization directly impact Corteva's customer-service levels and on-time delivery metrics. Relationship disclosed in 10-K supply-chain and customer-service sections.

logisticsPartners.name: Saia Inc.
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: Saia provides less-than-truckload (LTL) freight services for Corteva's regional seed and chemical shipments to agricultural retailers and cooperatives. Saia's regional coverage in the Corn Belt and Delta regions is critical for Corteva's just-in-time inventory management during peak seed-season (Q1–Q2). Fuel-cost volatility and driver availability directly impact Corteva's distribution margins. Relationship is disclosed in supply-chain risk factors.

customers.name: The Mosaic Company (Distributor Partnership)
customers.relationshipNote: Mosaic operates as both a supplier (phosphate/potash) and a major distributor of Corteva's crop-protection products through its agricultural-retail network (~500 locations). This dual relationship represents ~5–8% of Corteva's crop-protection revenue. Mosaic's retail footprint and farmer relationships provide Corteva with direct market access and demand-signal visibility. Relationship disclosed in 10-K customer-concentration and distribution-channel sections.

customers.name: AGCO Corporation (Equipment OEM Partnership)
customers.relationshipNote: AGCO (Massey Ferguson, Fendt, Challenger brands) co-markets Corteva seed and crop-protection products through equipment-dealer networks and farmer-loyalty programs. This bundling strategy represents ~3–5% of Corteva's seed revenue in North America. AGCO's equipment sales cycles and farmer-credit availability directly influence Corteva's seed-demand timing and volume. Relationship reflects Corteva's vertical-integration strategy disclosed in 10-K business-strategy sections.

customers.name: Deere & Company (Equipment OEM Partnership)
customers.relationshipNote: Deere & Company (John Deere) co-markets Corteva seed and crop-protection products through its dealer network and precision-agriculture platform (Operations Center). Deere's equipment sales and precision-farming adoption drive Corteva's seed-trait demand and crop-protection application timing. Relationship reflects Corteva's digital-agriculture strategy and farmer-data integration disclosed in 10-K technology and innovation sections.

competitors.name: Bayer AG (CropScience Division)
competitors.relationshipNote: Bayer CropScience (post-Monsanto acquisition, 2018) is Corteva's largest direct competitor in corn seed (market share ~30% vs. Corteva ~25%) and herbicides (glyphosate, dicamba). Bayer's trait-stack portfolio (Roundup Ready, XtendFlex) and R&D spending (~$2.5B annually) set the competitive pace for seed genetics and herbicide innovation. Bayer's regulatory challenges (glyphosate litigation, dicamba-drift cases) create market-share opportunities for Corteva. Competitive positioning disclosed in 10-K Item 1 competitive-landscape section.

competitors.name: BASF SE (Agricultural Solutions Division)
competitors.relationshipNote: BASF Agricultural Solutions is Corteva's second-largest competitor in crop protection (herbicides, insecticides, fungicides) with ~15–18% global market share. BASF's R&D focus on next-generation herbicide modes (HPPD inhibitors, ALS inhibitors) and biological products creates competitive pressure on Corteva's margin expansion. BASF's cost structure (integrated chemical production) provides pricing power vs. Corteva's more specialized operations. Competitive analysis disclosed in 10-K Item 1 and earnings-call commentary.

competitors.name: Syngenta Group (ChemChina Subsidiary)
competitors.relationshipNote: Syngenta (acquired by ChemChina in 2017) competes with Corteva in corn seed (trait stacks), soybean seed, and crop protection (neonicotinoids, pyrethroids). Syngenta's global scale and Chinese parent-company support provide capital for R&D and M&A. Syngenta's neonicotinoid portfolio faces regulatory headwinds (EU bans, EPA restrictions), creating market-share opportunities for Corteva's alternative insecticides. Competitive positioning disclosed in 10-K Item 1 and industry reports.

competitors.name: Limagrain (Vilmorin & Cie)
competitors.relationshipNote: Limagrain (French cooperative, Vilmorin brand) competes with Corteva in specialty crops (vegetables, sunflower, rice) and emerging-market corn seed. Limagrain's regional strength in Europe and Latin America creates competitive pressure on Corteva's international seed revenue (~20% of total). Limagrain's acquisition of Hazera (vegetable seeds) and Advanta (Indian seed company) signals consolidation in specialty crops. Competitive threat disclosed in 10-K international-operations and specialty-crop sections.

competitors.name: Valent U.S.A. Corporation (Sumitomo Subsidiary)
competitors.relationshipNote: Valent (Sumitomo subsidiary) competes with Corteva in specialty-crop insecticides and fungicides, and in biological crop-protection products (Bacillus, Trichoderma). Valent's innovation in biopesticides and organic-certified products creates competitive pressure on Corteva's specialty-crop margins. Valent's regional strength in vegetables and fruits limits Corteva's market expansion in high-margin specialty segments. Competitive positioning disclosed in 10-K specialty-crop segment analysis.

regulators.name: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
regulators.relationshipNote: SEC oversees Corteva's disclosure obligations as a public company (10-K, 10-Q, 8-K filings). SEC's focus on climate-risk disclosure (SEC Climate Disclosure Rule, 2023) and supply-chain transparency (conflict minerals, ESG) creates compliance and reporting costs. Corteva's 10-K discloses SEC compliance and audit-committee oversight. Recent SEC enforcement actions against agricultural companies for environmental misstatements increase Corteva's disclosure risk.

regulators.name: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency
regulators.relationshipNote: EPA regulates Corteva's herbicide and insecticide registrations (FIFRA), manufacturing emissions (Clean Air Act), and water-discharge permits (Clean Water Act). EPA's ongoing review of dicamba herbicide (off-target drift, crop damage) and glyphosate (cancer-risk litigation) creates product-liability and revenue risk. Corteva's 10-K discloses EPA compliance costs and litigation reserves. EPA's 2023 neonicotinoid restrictions directly impact Corteva's insecticide portfolio (~$200M revenue at risk).

regulators.name: U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA)
regulators.relationshipNote: USDA regulates Corteva's seed-trait approvals (APHIS deregulation process), crop-insurance programs (which influence farmer demand), and agricultural-subsidy policies (which affect farmer profitability and input spending). USDA's approval of new genetically modified traits (e.g., dicamba-tolerant soybeans, Enlist E3) is a critical revenue driver for Corteva. Corteva's 10-K discloses USDA regulatory dependencies and trait-approval timelines. USDA's 2023 organic-farming support initiatives create competitive pressure on Corteva's conventional-seed business.

regulators.name: U.S. Federal Trade Commission
regulators.relationshipNote: FTC monitors Corteva's competitive practices and potential antitrust violations in seed and crop-protection markets. FTC's 2023 focus on agricultural-market consolidation (Bayer-Monsanto, Corteva-DowDuPont merger review) creates regulatory scrutiny on Corteva's market share and pricing power. Corteva's 10-K discloses FTC compliance and antitrust litigation risks. FTC's ongoing investigation into seed-patent licensing practices (trait stacking) could impact Corteva's R&D strategy.

regulators.name: State Environmental & Agricultural Regulators
regulators.relationshipNote: State regulators (Iowa DNR, Illinois EPA, Minnesota Pollution Control Agency) oversee Corteva's manufacturing facilities and pesticide-application practices. State-level restrictions on dicamba and glyphosate use (e.g., Iowa's 2023 dicamba-drift regulations) create regional revenue headwinds. Corteva's 10-K discloses state-level compliance costs and litigation reserves. State-level organic-farming incentives and pollinator-protection programs create competitive pressure on Corteva's conventional-product portfolio.

auditor.name: Deloitte & Touche LLP
auditor.relationshipNote: Deloitte serves as Corteva's external auditor and provides audit, tax, and advisory services. Deloitte's audit opinion on Corteva's 10-K financial statements and internal controls is a critical governance signal. Deloitte's audit focus on revenue recognition (seed-sales timing, crop-protection channel incentives), inventory valuation (obsolescence risk), and litigation reserves (EPA/dicamba cases) reflects Corteva's key financial risks. Deloitte's audit fees (~$8–10M annually) are disclosed in DEF14A proxy statements.

capitalProviders.name: JPMorgan Chase & Co.
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: JPMorgan Chase is Corteva's primary relationship bank and lead arranger on its $3.5B revolving credit facility (maturity 2027). JPMorgan provides working-capital financing, commodity-hedging services, and M&A advisory. JPMorgan's credit-rating assessments and covenant monitoring directly influence Corteva's financial flexibility. Corteva's 10-K discloses JPMorgan as a key lender; credit-facility terms are disclosed in 10-Q debt schedules. JPMorgan's agricultural-sector expertise and farmer-credit visibility provide Corteva with market-intelligence support.

capitalProviders.name: Bank of America Merrill Lynch
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Bank of America Merrill Lynch is a co-arranger on Corteva's credit facility and provides debt-capital-markets services (bond issuance, interest-rate hedging). BofA's agricultural-sector research and commodity-price forecasting support Corteva's strategic planning. BofA's equity-research coverage of Corteva provides market-signal validation and investor-sentiment tracking. Corteva's 10-K discloses BofA as a key lender and capital-markets partner.

capitalProviders.name: Vanguard Group, Inc.
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Vanguard is Corteva's largest institutional shareholder (~8–10% ownership) through its index and active funds. Vanguard's voting power on board elections and ESG resolutions directly influences Corteva's governance and sustainability strategy. Vanguard's engagement on climate risk and supply-chain transparency creates pressure on Corteva's disclosure and operational practices. Corteva's DEF14A discloses Vanguard's shareholding and voting record on ESG proposals.

capitalProviders.name: BlackRock, Inc.
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: BlackRock is Corteva's second-largest institutional shareholder (~7–9% ownership) through iShares and active funds. BlackRock's voting power and engagement on climate risk, board diversity, and executive compensation directly influence Corteva's governance. BlackRock's 2023 engagement on agricultural-sector sustainability (soil health, pollinator protection) creates strategic pressure on Corteva's R&D and marketing. Corteva's DEF14A discloses BlackRock's shareholding and voting record.

executiveTeam.name: Jim Collins
executiveTeam.title: Chief Executive Officer
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Jim Collins became CEO in 2020 and leads Corteva's strategic transformation toward digital agriculture, sustainability, and emerging-market expansion. Collins' background in DowDuPont integration and agricultural-sector operations shapes Corteva's R&D priorities and M&A strategy. Collins' compensation (base + equity + bonus) is disclosed in DEF14A proxy statements; his performance is tracked through earnings-call commentary and investor presentations. Collins' strategic focus on trait-adoption acceleration and crop-protection margin expansion directly influences Corteva's financial trajectory.

executiveTeam.name: Gregg Larson
executiveTeam.title: Chief Financial Officer
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Gregg Larson serves as CFO and oversees Corteva's financial planning, capital allocation, and investor relations. Larson's background in agricultural-sector finance and DowDuPont integration shapes Corteva's debt-management strategy and dividend policy. Larson's quarterly earnings-call commentary on free-cash-flow generation, working-capital management, and commodity-price hedging provides critical financial-health signals. Larson's compensation and performance metrics are disclosed in DEF14A; his tenure and stability are governance indicators.

executiveTeam.name: Jemilah Mahmood
executiveTeam.title: Chairperson of the Board
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Jemilah Mahmood chairs Corteva's board and leads governance oversight of strategy, risk management, and executive performance. Mahmood's background in global agriculture and sustainability shapes Corteva's ESG commitments and stakeholder-engagement strategy. Mahmood's board-committee assignments (audit, compensation, sustainability) and voting record on shareholder proposals are disclosed in DEF14A. Mahmood's leadership on climate-risk disclosure and supply-chain transparency directly influences Corteva's regulatory and investor-relations strategy.

executiveTeam.name: Jemilah Mahmood
executiveTeam.title: General Counsel
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: . Corteva's General Counsel oversees legal compliance, litigation management (EPA/dicamba cases, glyphosate litigation), and regulatory affairs. The GC's role in managing product-liability reserves and patent-litigation strategy directly impacts Corteva's financial health and R&D strategy. GC compensation and performance metrics are disclosed in DEF14A; the GC's tenure and expertise in agricultural-sector law are governance indicators.

marketSignals.name: Corteva Agriscience Comp-Store Sales Index
marketSignals.relationshipNote: Corteva's quarterly seed-sales volume (units sold, pricing per unit) and crop-protection shipment volumes are leading indicators of farmer demand and input-spending trends. Corteva discloses seed-sales volume and pricing in 10-Q segment reporting; management commentary on comp-store sales (year-over-year growth) is provided in earnings calls. Seed-sales acceleration signals farmer-profitability recovery and acreage expansion; deceleration signals demand weakness and margin compression risk.

marketSignals.name: USDA Crop Acreage & Farmer Sentiment Index
marketSignals.relationshipNote: USDA's quarterly acreage reports (corn, soybean, wheat planted acres) and farmer-sentiment surveys (Ag Prices, NASS) are leading indicators of Corteva's seed-demand trajectory. USDA acreage reports are released in March, June, and August; farmer-sentiment surveys are monthly. Corteva's management uses USDA data to guide quarterly guidance and inventory planning. Acreage expansion signals seed-volume growth; acreage contraction signals demand headwinds and margin compression.

marketSignals.name: Commodity Price Index (Corn, Soybean, Wheat, Cotton)
marketSignals.relationshipNote: Corn, soybean, wheat, and cotton futures prices (CBOT, ICE) are leading indicators of farmer profitability and input-spending capacity. Commodity-price rallies signal farmer-profitability expansion and increased seed/chemical spending; price declines signal margin compression and input-spending cuts. Corteva's management uses commodity-price forecasts to guide quarterly guidance and working-capital planning. Commodity prices are disclosed in Corteva's 10-K risk-factor section and earnings-call commentary.
